newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev rise halts at 1,520-1,525 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev rise halts at 1,520-1,525 per dollar.

text.p: A rise in dollar demand halted a lev rise at 1,520-1,525 per dollar at Tuesday's close from the opening's 1,570-1,580 but the market remained dollar-bearish as investors eyed high-yield local debt, dealers said.
"A large final client started bidding for dollars in the afternoon, consolidating trade between 1,520-1,530 levs per dollar," a commercial bank dealer said.
"The lev closed at 1,520-1,525 but it could have gained further if dollar demand had not risen," the dealer added.
Foreign investors were buying mainly government securities with maturity of six months or longer as this type of paper is considered a foreign investment under Bulgarian law, traders said.
Effective annual yield on six-month floater coupon T-bills auctioned on Monday was 132.77 percent and 12-month floater coupon paper yielded 108.48 percent, central bank figures showed.

The lev recovered from Monday's lows of 1,630 as investors in lev-denominated instruments regained confidence from Finance minister's comments that the lev fall was highly speculative and there were no fundamental reasons for it.
A rise in central bank reserves to 1.09 billion on April 21 from 554.3 million at end March also lent support to the lev.

Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said it was not true that the interim government has kept the lev stable between 1,500-1,600 since early March through administrative means just to win Saturday's election.
"Bulgaria has secured enough foreign funding to meet its foreign debt payments this year," Gavriiski said on Monday.

With all but a few results from Saturday's poll counted the pro-reform Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) has won 52 percent of the vote or 137 seats in the 240-seat parliament. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
